Dropped claims are logged with the reason. - A cause of death is stated only as printed. - The link between a ghost and a death is graded strong, possible or weak, with its reasons listed (name match, place match, date gap). - **Output:** a `cases` document, plus one Sentry trace per case with a span per step carrying model, tokens, cost and latency. - **Budgets:** a maximum number of steps per case, a maximum number of web searches per case, and a global SerpApi counter (the free plan is 250 searches a month). ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant W as InvestigateCase workflow participant M as Model activity participant T as Tool activities W->>M: step 1, plan (result recorded) W->>T: step 2, search_archive and find_death_notices (recorded) Note over W: worker killed here W-->>W: replay from history: steps 1 and 2 reuse recorded results W->>M: step 3, write claims W->>T: step 4, verify quotes and save the case file ``` ### 3.6 Static export and the site - `export_static` reads Atlas and writes: - `front.json`: printed-on-this-night candidates, ticker headlines and totals - `towns/index.json`: a compact town index for search on the device - `towns/{place_id}.json` and `cases/{report_id}.json` - `reel.json`: the archive chart - The API contract is in `SRS.md` section 6. - Both services are defined in `render.yaml`. Nothing deploys until the owner says yes. ## 4. Data model (MongoDB Atlas, database `paperghosts`) Pydantic models in the Python package are the single source of truth. Atlas JSON Schema validators are generated from them. **`reports`:** one document per story. - `_id`, plus `primary_article_id` - `printings[]`: article ID, LCCN, paper title, publication place, state, date, scan location, `bbox_list`, crop URLs - `headline`, `text` (the OCR of the primary printing), `date` (earliest printing), `year`, `month_day` - `kind` (always `report` in this collection) - `fields`: each is `{value, quote, verified, score}`: - `place` - `people[]` - `seen` - `outcome`: unexplained, explained, hoax or unknown - `specific_place` - `place_type`: house, church, cemetery, inn or hotel, road or bridge, public building, ship, or other - `precision`: town, street or building - `location`: GeoJSON point, with `location_precision` and `location_source` - `place_id`, `town`, `state` - `embedding` - `reader`: model, adapter version, prompt version - `lexicon_terms[]` - `case_id`, when an investigation exists **`places`:** GeoNames ID, name, alternate names, state, location, report count, first and last year. **`cases`:** - `report_id` - `claims[]`: each with its text, the clippings it cites (article ID, quote, verified) and a confidence - `followups[]`: each with its relation (follow-up, debunking, arrest, moved out, inquest or death notice), date, paper, quote and crop URLs - `person`: name, death-notice article, link grade and reasons - `then_now`: the "then" side; the "now" items, each with source, URL, retrieval date and quote; and differences, each backed by both quotes - `run`: model, provider, steps, tokens, cost, latency, Sentry trace ID and Temporal workflow ID **`stats`:** one document per year and per state: pages, articles, candidates, stories, printings, and reports per million articles. **Indexes:** - `reports`: - a 2dsphere index on `location` - compound `{place_id, date}` and `{month_day}` - an Atlas Search index on headline, text, field values and town, used with fuzzy matching - a Vector Search index on `embedding`, with filters on state and decade - `places`: 2dsphere, plus Atlas Search autocomplete on names - `cases`: `{report_id}` **Storage budget:** if the cluster is the free tier (512 MB), only stories, places, cases and stats go to Atlas. Candidates and reader outputs stay local, and the article says so. The real per-document size is measured in Phase 2B before anything is loaded. ## 5. Repo layout ``` Makefile setup, keys, temporal, worker, smoke, ingest, eval, db-init, db-verify, api, web, app, test, lint, numbers pyproject.toml one uv project, Python pinned in .python-version paperghosts/ the Python package config.py reads .env; never prints a value schemas/ Pydantic models (single source of truth) ingest/ streaming reader, lexicon, prefilter, samples reader/ prompts, Tinker training and sampling, local runner, quote verifier geo/ GeoNames loader, LCCN title parser, geocoder cluster/ reprint clustering, embeddings store/ Atlas loader, indexes, validators, static export investigator/ agent loop, tools, guardrails workflows/ Temporal workflows, activities, worker observability/ Sentry setup and model-call spans api/ FastAPI app (read-only) web/ React + Vite + TypeScript site and design system eval/ gold/ split, hash, labelling policy (committed) results/ JSON and charts for evals A to D (committed) scripts/ one-off checks: keys, crop check, offline proof, numbers sheet tests/ unit, integration (Temporal test env), API contract data/ local only, gitignored except small manifests Docs/ BRIEF, ARCHITECTURE, PRD, SRS, BUILD-PLAN, DECISIONS, RESUME, UI-IDEAS (IDEAS.md stays private) .github/workflows/ CI render.yaml deploy blueprint (used only after the owner's yes) ``` ## 6. Environments and delivery - **Local:** `make temporal`, `make worker`, `make api` and `make web` run everything on the owner's machine. - **CI (GitHub Actions):** lint, offline tests, a web typecheck and build, and a secret scan, on every push and pull request. CI needs no secrets; tests that need the network are marked and skipped there. - **CD (Render):** a Blueprint with an API web service and a static site. It auto-deploys from `main` only after the owner approves the first deploy. - Render environment variables are set by the owner. - Atlas network access must allow Render's servers; that change also needs the owner's yes. - **Releases:** Sentry releases are tagged with the git SHA. ## 7. Security and privacy - **Secrets:** - Secrets reach code only through environment variables. - `config.py` redacts them in `repr`, logs and errors. - The Ultramarine key is named `PAPERINSTRUMENTS_API_KEY` in `.env`; config also accepts `ULTRAMARINE_API_KEY`. - **Sentry:** `send_default_pii=False`, and a `before_send` hook strips coordinates and query strings. - **Near me:** coordinates are rounded to about 1 km on the device and again on the server, used for that one query, and never logged. - **Secret scanning:** a scanner runs in CI. - Entire is on with telemetry off, and its checkpoints sync to the private `origin`. - Before the repo goes public, the Entire checkpoint refs and the recorded sessions are scanned for secrets. - **The people in the archive:** nobody is named except as the papers printed them, and nothing about how they died is guessed. ## 8. Architecture risks and what answers them | Risk | Answer | |---|---| | Ingest is limited by CPU, not network | Measure parse speed in Phase 1 and set concurrency from it | | Too many candidates for the reader budget | A triage stage measured for recall, plus cost per 10,000 articles and a Tinker credit check before the full pass | | Reprints inflate counts and leak gold into training | Reprint clustering, counts labelled as stories or printings, and a leakage check script | | Rough OCR | Fuzzy quote verification, and optionally Gemma re-reading the scan image when the OCR is unreadable | | LoC image service is slow or down | Lazy loading, cached crops for the top content, and a text fallback | | Render free services sleep | The core path is served from static JSON | | Atlas free tier is 512 MB | Only stories go to Atlas; the bulk stays local and the article says so | | Gemma 4 26B on 24 GB of RAM | Never run it alongside the local student; measure tokens per second in Phase 1 |

1	# SRS: Paper Ghosts
2	
3	Software requirements, each with an ID and how it is verified. The gates in `BUILD-PLAN.md` check against these IDs. The product view is in `PRD.md`, and the design is in `ARCHITECTURE.md`.
4	
5	## 1. Definitions
6	- **Article:** one article region from AmericanStories, with its text, headline, bounding boxes and page.
7	- **Printing:** one article as printed in one paper on one date.
8	- **Story:** a cluster of printings of the same text. Syndicated stories were reprinted in many papers.
9	- **Candidate:** an article that hit the lexicon.
10	- **Report:** a candidate the reader classified as `kind = report`.
11	- **Case:** a report the investigator worked on.
12	- **Clipping:** the crop of the page scan for one article.
13	- **Verified quote:** a quote the verifier found in the source text, within the calibrated fuzzy threshold.
14	- **Precision:** how exactly a location is known: town, street or building.
15	
16	## 2. Functional requirements
17	
18	### 2.1 Ingest (ING)
19	| ID | Requirement | Verified by |
20	|---|---|---|
21	| ING-1 | All 180 year files are streamed without ever storing a tarball. Ingest outputs total at most 10 GB on disk. | Per-year manifests, and a disk-use line in eval A |
22	| ING-2 | Each year file is one Temporal activity, with heartbeats and a retry policy. Outputs are idempotent. | The Temporal UI history, and kill test 1 |
23	| ING-3 | The lexicon is versioned in code, covers common OCR variants, and each candidate records the terms it matched. | Unit tests, including OCR-variant cases |
24	| ING-4 | Each year records its pages, articles and candidates, by state and by term. | `eval/results/archive_read.json` |
25	| ING-5 | Each year writes a random non-candidate sample and a near-miss pool. | Files exist, and eval A has a recall section |
26	| ING-6 | The crop builder handles single-column and multi-column articles (`bbox_list`). It is checked on 50 random candidates spread across as many batches as the sample allows. | `eval/results/crop_check.json`, plus a contact sheet image |
27	
28	### 2.2 Reader (RDR)
29	| ID | Requirement | Verified by |
30	|---|---|---|
31	| RDR-1 | The gold set has 150–300 articles, stratified by decade and term. It is frozen and hashed before training, and the split is committed. | `eval/gold/split.json` and `eval/gold/HASH`, unchanged in git history after the freeze |
32	| RDR-2 | The label schema covers: `kind` (report, fiction, idiom, religious, advert, other); place, people, seen and outcome (unexplained, explained, hoax, unknown); and, for walks, specific place, place type (house, church, cemetery, inn or hotel, road or bridge, public building, ship, other) and precision. Each value carries a verbatim quote. | Schema tests |
33	| RDR-3 | `eval/gold/POLICY.md` holds the rules for hard cases and is written before any labelling. | Git history order |
34	| RDR-4 | Training data is disjoint from the gold set, including reprints of gold stories. | `scripts/check_leakage.py` exits 0 |
35	| RDR-5 | LoRA training runs on Tinker. The configs, checkpoints and seeds are recorded. | `eval/results/reader_runs.json` |
36	| RDR-6 | Eval B compares base 4B, tuned 4B and the teacher on the gold set. It reports metrics with bootstrap 95% intervals, cost per 10,000 articles, and p50 and p95 latency. | `eval/results/reader_eval.json`, plus charts |
37	| RDR-7 | Every ablation in section 7.2 is run, or its absence is explained. | Ablation JSON and charts |
38	| RDR-8 | The edge-case suite in section 7.3 is reported slice by slice. | `eval/results/reader_edge_cases.json` |
39	| RDR-9 | The quote verifier's threshold is calibrated on the gold set. A field whose quote doesn't verify becomes "not stated". | Calibration curve, plus unit tests |
40	| RDR-10 | The tuned student runs locally with no network, on at least 200 articles, and its agreement with the Tinker-served outputs is reported. A guard in the runner blocks sockets, so system network settings are never touched. | `scripts/offline_proof.py` output |
41	| RDR-11 | The full reader pass covers every triaged candidate, and its outputs are versioned. | Counts in eval A and B |
42	| RDR-12 | At least one failure the eval exposed is logged, with what changed because of it. | `DECISIONS.md`, and the README failure log |
43	
44	### 2.3 Places (GEO)
45	| ID | Requirement | Verified by |
46	|---|---|---|
47	| GEO-1 | The publication place is parsed from the LCCN title and geocoded offline against GeoNames `cities1000`. A manifest records the source, retrieval date and licence. | Parser tests on at least 200 distinct titles, plus the manifest |
48	| GEO-2 | Every location carries its precision and source. Street or building coordinates exist only when a source supplies them. | Schema validator, plus a test |
49	| GEO-3 | When a place name is ambiguous, the state from the article or the paper decides. A place that can't be resolved gets no pin and is listed. | Tests, plus an unresolved-places report |
50	
51	### 2.4 Data layer (DB)
52	| ID | Requirement | Verified by |
53	|---|---|---|
54	| DB-1 | Collections and JSON Schema validators are generated from the Pydantic models (`ARCHITECTURE.md` section 4). | `make db-init` is idempotent |
55	| DB-2 | Indexes exist: 2dsphere, Atlas Search with fuzzy matching, Vector Search, and compound indexes. | `make db-verify` |
56	| DB-3 | Storage stays within the cluster limit, and what stays local is documented. | A storage report in eval A |
57	| DB-4 | Printings are clustered into stories, and the cluster precision is measured on a labelled sample of at least 100 pairs. | `eval/results/clustering.json` |
58	| DB-5 | The loader upserts by stable IDs, so re-running it changes nothing. | Integration test |
59	| DB-6 | Geo, fuzzy and vector queries return the expected results, and their latencies are recorded. Example: a search for "appariiion" finds "apparition". | `make db-verify` output |
60	
61	### 2.5 Investigator (INV)
62	| ID | Requirement | Verified by |
63	|---|---|---|
64	| INV-1 | The rule that picks the top cases is written down and versioned. | The code, plus `DECISIONS.md` |
65	| INV-2 | The follow-up harvest runs on Temporal and streams each needed year file once. | Workflow history, plus manifests |
66	| INV-3 | Every model call and every tool call is an activity with an idempotency key and a budget cap. | Code review, plus workflow history |
67	| INV-4 | A claim is kept only if its citations verify. Dropped claims are logged with the reason. | Each case's `drops` log, plus an audit |
68	| INV-5 | A person link shows both clippings, a grade and its reasons. No cause of death is stated beyond what was printed. | An audit of every person link |
69	| INV-6 | Each "now" item comes from SerpApi, or from Wikipedia with a label saying so, and carries its URL and retrieval date. A difference is recorded only when both quotes exist. | Schema, plus an audit |
70	| INV-7 | Kill test 2: the worker is killed mid-investigation, and the workflow resumes at the same step. No completed paid call is repeated. A call that was in flight at the moment of the kill is retried, and the test reports how many there were. | Temporal UI screenshots, plus call counters from the providers and from activity logs |
71	| INV-8 | Each case run produces one Sentry trace, with spans for model calls carrying model, tokens, cost and latency. | Trace links, plus numbers pulled with `SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN` |
72	| INV-9 | Ultramarine runs on the same cases as the default model, and its actual cost is recorded. | `eval/results/investigator_compare.json` |
73	| INV-10 | Eval C counts case files, named deaths, cases explained or exposed, and then-and-now differences. | `eval/results/investigations.json` |
74	
75	### 2.6 API (API)
76	| ID | Requirement | Verified by |
77	|---|---|---|
78	| API-1 | The endpoints in section 6 are implemented with input validation, pagination and a consistent error format. | Contract tests |
79	| API-2 | `/api/near` rounds coordinates to 2 decimal places, never logs them, and keeps them out of Sentry. | A test with a log-capture fixture |
80	| API-3 | CORS allows only the site's own origins. Responses carry cache headers. | Tests |
81	| API-4 | `/api/health` reports whether Atlas is reachable. Sentry is wired up with no PII. | Test, plus a Sentry event |
82	| API-5 | p95 latency is measured for every endpoint against Atlas. | `eval/results/api_latency.json` |
83	
84	### 2.7 Web (WEB)
85	| ID | Requirement | Verified by |
86	|---|---|---|
87	| WEB-1 | The pages are: front page, town drawer, case, the reel, the method page, a 404 ("This page was never filed."), and walks if they are built. | Playwright e2e |
88	| WEB-2 | The design system covers tokens, type, components and brand assets (`BUILD-PLAN.md`, Phase 4A). A style-guide route shows every component, using real archive data only. | Screenshots of the style guide in both modes and at phone width |
89	| WEB-3 | The pull-chain switches lights on and off. The default follows the device setting and the time. | e2e |
90	| WEB-4 | The seven signature moments from `UI-IDEAS.md` are built, each with its reduced-motion fallback. | e2e with reduced motion emulated |
91	| WEB-5 | Layouts are phone-first, and clipping crops are lazy-loaded. The first clipping is the LCP element. | Lighthouse |
92	| WEB-6 | Each clipping's alt text is its transcription. | e2e |
93	| WEB-7 | UI copy follows the voice rules, and a lint script fails the build on banned words. | `make lint` |
94	| WEB-8 | Fonts are self-hosted, so no request goes to Google. | The e2e network log |
95	| WEB-9 | The map uses MapLibre with OpenFreeMap tiles and a muted atlas style. Pins show precision: a ring for a town, a line for a street, a square for a building. | Screenshot, plus a unit test of the pin choice |
96	| WEB-10 | Every data view has loading, empty and error states. A sleeping API changes only the live features. | e2e with the API stubbed down |
97	
98	### 2.8 Walks (WALK, P2)
99	| ID | Requirement | Verified by |
100	|---|---|---|
101	| WALK-1 | A walk has at least 3 public stops, located at street or building precision, all within about 3 km. A private home is never a stop. | Generator tests |
102	| WALK-2 | Whether each stop still stands is checked through SerpApi Maps, and only checked stops are counted. | Eval D counts |
103	| WALK-3 | The assignment sheet prints cleanly and works offline. | A print-to-PDF snapshot |
104	
105	## 3. Non-functional requirements
106	| ID | Requirement | Verified by |
107	|---|---|---|
108	| NFR-SEC-1 | No secret appears in the repo, in logs, or in recorded sessions. A secret scanner runs in CI, and the Entire checkpoints are scanned before the repo goes public. | CI, plus a scan report |
109	| NFR-SEC-2 | API input validation, a simple rate limit, and a dependency audit. | Tests, plus an audit report |
110	| NFR-PRIV-1 | No accounts, no tracking analytics and no session replay. The only thing stored on the device is the lights preference. | Code review, plus the e2e network log |
111	| NFR-REL-1 | The ingest and the investigation both survive a killed worker (kill tests 1 and 2). | Screenshots, plus counters |
112	| NFR-PERF-1 | Core Web Vitals are "good" on a mid-range phone profile. Initial JS stays under 200 KB gzipped, with the map loaded lazily. | Lighthouse, plus a bundle report |
113	| NFR-A11Y-1 | WCAG 2.2 AA: reading-text contrast of at least 4.5:1 in both modes, a visible blue-pencil focus style, full keyboard use, reduced motion respected, semantic headings. | axe, a contrast script, plus a keyboard e2e test |
114	| NFR-REPRO-1 | Every number shown anywhere comes from a script. `make numbers` regenerates the numbers sheet, with the command behind each number. | The numbers sheet diffs clean |
115	| NFR-COST-1 | Only free tiers and existing credits are used. Every run logs its cost. SerpApi use stays within budget. | Cost logs |
116	| NFR-OBS-1 | Both Sentry projects receive events, and releases are tagged with the git SHA. | The Sentry API |
117	| NFR-TEST-1 | Unit tests (lexicon, crop URLs, quote verifier, geocoder, schemas), integration tests (Temporal test environment), contract tests (API) and e2e tests (Playwright) all run from `make test`. | CI |
118	| NFR-LIC-1 | AmericanStories (CC-BY-4.0), GeoNames (CC-BY), the LoC scans, the OpenStreetMap and OpenFreeMap attribution, the font licences and the React Bits licence are all credited on the method page and in the README. | Review |
119	
120	## 4. Constraints
121	- **Machine:** Apple M4 with 10 cores, 24 GB of RAM, and about 35 GB of free disk (measured Oct 29). No Docker.
122	- **Installed tools:** `uv`, Node and `pnpm`, the Temporal CLI with its dev server, Ollama (with `gemma4:26b-a4b-it-qat` and smaller Gemma 4 variants already pulled), `gh` and `entire`. Nothing is installed globally; project dependencies go through `uv` and `pnpm`.
123	- **Keys:** `.env` holds them; check them by shape only. The names are listed in `BRIEF.md`; the Ultramarine key is `PAPERINSTRUMENTS_API_KEY`. `GEMINI_API_KEY`, `ELEVENLABS_API_KEY` and `TABPFN_TOKEN` are present but unused.
124	- **Atlas:** the existing cluster. Its tier and storage limit are recorded in Phase 1.
125	
126	## 5. Data requirements
127	- **Schemas:** `ARCHITECTURE.md` section 4. Pydantic is the source; Atlas validators are generated from it.
128	- **Stable IDs:**
129	  - A report is `r_` plus its primary article ID.
130	  - A case is `c_` plus its report ID.
131	  - A place is its GeoNames ID.
132	- **Every derived record** carries the versions that made it (lexicon, prompt, model or adapter, code SHA).
133	- **Dates** are ISO 8601. `month_day` is `MM-DD`, used by "Printed on this night".
134	- **Text:** the OCR text is stored as printed and is never corrected in place. A cleaned transcription, if one is shown, is stored separately and labelled.
135	
136	## 6. API contract (read-only)
137	| Method and path | Returns |
138	|---|---|
139	| `GET /api/health` | `{ok, atlas, version}` |
140	| `GET /api/places?q=&state=` | Matching towns: `{place_id, name, state, report_count, years}` |
141	| `GET /api/towns/{place_id}` | The drawer: the place, its count line, and its reports `{id, date, paper, label, outcome, precision, location}` |
142	| `GET /api/reports/{id}` | The full case page payload: the report, plus its case if one exists |
143	| `GET /api/search?q=&state=&decade=&page=` | Text-search hits with a snippet, and the misread spellings each hit matched, e.g. `{scanned: "appariiion", term: "apparition"}` |
144	| `GET /api/near?lat=&lon=&km=` | Reports near a rounded point. The coordinates are never logged. |
145	| `GET /api/reports/{id}/similar?k=` | Vector-search neighbours |
146	| `GET /api/tonight?md=MM-DD` | Reports printed on that month and day |
147	| `GET /api/stats/reel` | Per-year and per-state series |
148	| `GET /api/walks/{place_id}` | A walk (P2 only) |
149	
150	Errors take the form `{"error": {"code", "message"}}`. The core path is mirrored as static JSON (`ARCHITECTURE.md` section 3.6), so the site works while the API sleeps.
151	
152	## 7. Evaluation specifications
153	Results are saved as JSON plus a chart under `eval/results/`, and each is produced by one command.
154	
155	### 7.1 Evals A to D
156	- **A, the archive read:**
157	  - pages and articles read, and candidates per year
158	  - reports per million articles, by year and by state
159	  - the term mix and an OCR-quality distribution
160	  - prefilter recall: a random-sample upper bound (rule of three when no misses are found) and the misses found in the near-miss pool, with the lexicon changes they caused
161	- **B, the reader:**
162	  - kind accuracy and macro-F1, and report precision, recall and F1
163	  - field match rates, and the share of quotes verified
164	  - the hallucinated-quote rate
165	  - cost per 10,000 articles and latency
166	  - bootstrap 95% intervals throughout
167	  - the headline is the accuracy gap and the cost per 10,000 articles
168	- **C, the investigations:** case files written, named deaths found, cases explained or exposed, then-and-now differences, the claim-verification rate and dropped claims, and Gemma against Ultramarine on the same cases (claims, verification rate, cost, latency).
169	- **D, the app:** Lighthouse on mobile, axe, contrast, e2e on phone and desktop in both modes, and the walks counts if walks are built.
170	
171	### 7.2 Reader ablations
172	| ID | What changes | Why it matters |
173	|---|---|---|
174	| B1 | Base 4B, tuned 4B, teacher | The headline comparison |
175	| B2 | Training set size (a learning curve of at least 3 points) | Whether more teacher labels would help |
176	| B3 | LoRA rank and learning rate (a small grid, within credits) | Picks the trained model |
177	| B4 | Output format: fields with quotes against kind only | The cost of grounding |
178	| B5 | Quote verifier on and off, plus a threshold sweep | Precision of the fields shown |
179	| B6 | Triage on and off | Reports lost against cost saved |
180	| B7 | Slices by OCR quality | Robustness to rough scans |
181	| B8 | Slices by decade | Language drift from 1774 to 1963 |
182	| B9 | Base 4B zero-shot against few-shot | Makes the baseline fair |
183	| B10 | Reprint leakage removed, or not | Proves the scores aren't inflated |
184	
185	Model selection uses a dev split. The gold set is used only for these final runs.
186	
187	### 7.3 Edge-case suite
188	Each slice uses at least 5 gold items where the archive has them:
189	- E1: sermons and hymns about the Holy Ghost
190	- E2: idioms ("ghost of a chance", "gave up the ghost", "not the ghost of a")
191	- E3: ghost stories as fiction, serials and Christmas stories
192	- E4: theatre and illusion adverts (Pepper's ghost), patent medicine and real estate
193	- E5: spiritualist séances and rappings (`POLICY.md` decides their kind)
194	- E6: hoax exposures and pranksters caught
195	- E7: humour and joke columns
196	- E8: phantom ships, trains and lights
197	- E9: one story reprinted under different datelines
198	- E10: badly garbled OCR
199	- E11: segmentation errors, where several items are merged into one article
200	- E12: non-English text
201	- E13: "Ghost" as a surname or a place name
202	- E14: political figures of speech ("the ghost of the tariff")
203	
204	## 8. Traceability
205	| Requirements | Phase | Evidence |
206	|---|---|---|
207	| Environment, CI, skeleton | 1 | `eval/results/phase1_env.json`, CI run, skeleton screenshot |
208	| ING-*, eval A | 2A | `eval/results/archive_read.json`, kill test 1, crop check |
209	| GEO-*, DB-1 to DB-3 | 2B | `make db-init`, storage report, parser tests |
210	| RDR-*, eval B | 2C | `eval/results/reader_*.json`, `eval/MODEL_CARD.md` |
211	| DB-4 to DB-6, INV-2 | 2D | `make db-verify`, `eval/results/clustering.json`, harvest manifests |
212	| INV-*, eval C | 3A | Case files, kill test 2, Sentry traces |
213	| API-* | 3B | Contract tests, `eval/results/api_latency.json` |
214	| WEB-*, NFR-A11Y, NFR-PERF | 4 | e2e, axe, Lighthouse, screenshots |
215	| NFR-*, the numbers sheet, launch | 5 | `make numbers`, README, scan report, the post draft |

# SRS: Paper Ghosts

Software requirements, each with an ID and how it is verified. The gates in `BUILD-PLAN.md` check against these IDs. The product view is in `PRD.md`, and the design is in `ARCHITECTURE.md`.

## 1. Definitions
- **Article:** one article region from AmericanStories, with its text, headline, bounding boxes and page.
- **Printing:** one article as printed in one paper on one date.
- **Story:** a cluster of printings of the same text. Syndicated stories were reprinted in many papers.
- **Candidate:** an article that hit the lexicon.
- **Report:** a candidate the reader classified as `kind = report`.
- **Case:** a report the investigator worked on.
- **Clipping:** the crop of the page scan for one article.
- **Verified quote:** a quote the verifier found in the source text, within the calibrated fuzzy threshold.
- **Precision:** how exactly a location is known: town, street or building.

## 2. Functional requirements

### 2.1 Ingest (ING)
| ID | Requirement | Verified by |
|---|---|---|
| ING-1 | All 180 year files are streamed without ever storing a tarball. Ingest outputs total at most 10 GB on disk. | Per-year manifests, and a disk-use line in eval A |
| ING-2 | Each year file is one Temporal activity, with heartbeats and a retry policy. Outputs are idempotent. | The Temporal UI history, and kill test 1 |
| ING-3 | The lexicon is versioned in code, covers common OCR variants, and each candidate records the terms it matched. | Unit tests, including OCR-variant cases |
| ING-4 | Each year records its pages, articles and candidates, by state and by term. | `eval/results/archive_read.json` |
| ING-5 | Each year writes a random non-candidate sample and a near-miss pool. | Files exist, and eval A has a recall section |
| ING-6 | The crop builder handles single-column and multi-column articles (`bbox_list`). It is checked on 50 random candidates spread across as many batches as the sample allows. | `eval/results/crop_check.json`, plus a contact sheet image |

### 2.2 Reader (RDR)
| ID | Requirement | Verified by |
|---|---|---|
| RDR-1 | The gold set has 150–300 articles, stratified by decade and term. It is frozen and hashed before training, and the split is committed. | `eval/gold/split.json` and `eval/gold/HASH`, unchanged in git history after the freeze |
| RDR-2 | The label schema covers: `kind` (report, fiction, idiom, religious, advert, other); place, people, seen and outcome (unexplained, explained, hoax, unknown); and, for walks, specific place, place type (house, church, cemetery, inn or hotel, road or bridge, public building, ship, other) and precision. Each value carries a verbatim quote. | Schema tests |
| RDR-3 | `eval/gold/POLICY.md` holds the rules for hard cases and is written before any labelling. | Git history order |
| RDR-4 | Training data is disjoint from the gold set, including reprints of gold stories. | `scripts/check_leakage.py` exits 0 |
| RDR-5 | LoRA training runs on Tinker. The configs, checkpoints and seeds are recorded. | `eval/results/reader_runs.json` |
| RDR-6 | Eval B compares base 4B, tuned 4B and the teacher on the gold set. It reports metrics with bootstrap 95% intervals, cost per 10,000 articles, and p50 and p95 latency. | `eval/results/reader_eval.json`, plus charts |
| RDR-7 | Every ablation in section 7.2 is run, or its absence is explained. | Ablation JSON and charts |
| RDR-8 | The edge-case suite in section 7.3 is reported slice by slice. | `eval/results/reader_edge_cases.json` |
| RDR-9 | The quote verifier's threshold is calibrated on the gold set. A field whose quote doesn't verify becomes "not stated". | Calibration curve, plus unit tests |
| RDR-10 | The tuned student runs locally with no network, on at least 200 articles, and its agreement with the Tinker-served outputs is reported. A guard in the runner blocks sockets, so system network settings are never touched. | `scripts/offline_proof.py` output |
| RDR-11 | The full reader pass covers every triaged candidate, and its outputs are versioned. | Counts in eval A and B |
| RDR-12 | At least one failure the eval exposed is logged, with what changed because of it. | `DECISIONS.md`, and the README failure log |

### 2.3 Places (GEO)
| ID | Requirement | Verified by |
|---|---|---|
| GEO-1 | The publication place is parsed from the LCCN title and geocoded offline against GeoNames `cities1000`. A manifest records the source, retrieval date and licence. | Parser tests on at least 200 distinct titles, plus the manifest |
| GEO-2 | Every location carries its precision and source. Street or building coordinates exist only when a source supplies them. | Schema validator, plus a test |
| GEO-3 | When a place name is ambiguous, the state from the article or the paper decides. A place that can't be resolved gets no pin and is listed. | Tests, plus an unresolved-places report |

### 2.4 Data layer (DB)
| ID | Requirement | Verified by |
|---|---|---|
| DB-1 | Collections and JSON Schema validators are generated from the Pydantic models (`ARCHITECTURE.md` section 4). | `make db-init` is idempotent |
| DB-2 | Indexes exist: 2dsphere, Atlas Search with fuzzy matching, Vector Search, and compound indexes. | `make db-verify` |
| DB-3 | Storage stays within the cluster limit, and what stays local is documented. | A storage report in eval A |
| DB-4 | Printings are clustered into stories, and the cluster precision is measured on a labelled sample of at least 100 pairs. | `eval/results/clustering.json` |
| DB-5 | The loader upserts by stable IDs, so re-running it changes nothing. | Integration test |
| DB-6 | Geo, fuzzy and vector queries return the expected results, and their latencies are recorded. Example: a search for "appariiion" finds "apparition". | `make db-verify` output |

### 2.5 Investigator (INV)
| ID | Requirement | Verified by |
|---|---|---|
| INV-1 | The rule that picks the top cases is written down and versioned. | The code, plus `DECISIONS.md` |
| INV-2 | The follow-up harvest runs on Temporal and streams each needed year file once. | Workflow history, plus manifests |
| INV-3 | Every model call and every tool call is an activity with an idempotency key and a budget cap. | Code review, plus workflow history |
| INV-4 | A claim is kept only if its citations verify. Dropped claims are logged with the reason. | Each case's `drops` log, plus an audit |
| INV-5 | A person link shows both clippings, a grade and its reasons. No cause of death is stated beyond what was printed. | An audit of every person link |
| INV-6 | Each "now" item comes from SerpApi, or from Wikipedia with a label saying so, and carries its URL and retrieval date. A difference is recorded only when both quotes exist. | Schema, plus an audit |
| INV-7 | Kill test 2: the worker is killed mid-investigation, and the workflow resumes at the same step. No completed paid call is repeated. A call that was in flight at the moment of the kill is retried, and the test reports how many there were. | Temporal UI screenshots, plus call counters from the providers and from activity logs |
| INV-8 | Each case run produces one Sentry trace, with spans for model calls carrying model, tokens, cost and latency. | Trace links, plus numbers pulled with `SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN` |
| INV-9 | Ultramarine runs on the same cases as the default model, and its actual cost is recorded. | `eval/results/investigator_compare.json` |
| INV-10 | Eval C counts case files, named deaths, cases explained or exposed, and then-and-now differences. | `eval/results/investigations.json` |

### 2.6 API (API)
| ID | Requirement | Verified by |
|---|---|---|
| API-1 | The endpoints in section 6 are implemented with input validation, pagination and a consistent error format. | Contract tests |
| API-2 | `/api/near` rounds coordinates to 2 decimal places, never logs them, and keeps them out of Sentry. | A test with a log-capture fixture |
| API-3 | CORS allows only the site's own origins. Responses carry cache headers. | Tests |
| API-4 | `/api/health` reports whether Atlas is reachable. Sentry is wired up with no PII. | Test, plus a Sentry event |
| API-5 | p95 latency is measured for every endpoint against Atlas. | `eval/results/api_latency.json` |

### 2.7 Web (WEB)
| ID | Requirement | Verified by |
|---|---|---|
| WEB-1 | The pages are: front page, town drawer, case, the reel, the method page, a 404 ("This page was never filed."), and walks if they are built. | Playwright e2e |
| WEB-2 | The design system covers tokens, type, components and brand assets (`BUILD-PLAN.md`, Phase 4A). A style-guide route shows every component, using real archive data only. | Screenshots of the style guide in both modes and at phone width |
| WEB-3 | The pull-chain switches lights on and off. The default follows the device setting and the time. | e2e |
| WEB-4 | The seven signature moments from `UI-IDEAS.md` are built, each with its reduced-motion fallback. | e2e with reduced motion emulated |
| WEB-5 | Layouts are phone-first, and clipping crops are lazy-loaded. The first clipping is the LCP element. | Lighthouse |
| WEB-6 | Each clipping's alt text is its transcription. | e2e |
| WEB-7 | UI copy follows the voice rules, and a lint script fails the build on banned words. | `make lint` |
| WEB-8 | Fonts are self-hosted, so no request goes to Google. | The e2e network log |
| WEB-9 | The map uses MapLibre with OpenFreeMap tiles and a muted atlas style. Pins show precision: a ring for a town, a line for a street, a square for a building. | Screenshot, plus a unit test of the pin choice |
| WEB-10 | Every data view has loading, empty and error states. A sleeping API changes only the live features. | e2e with the API stubbed down |

### 2.8 Walks (WALK, P2)
| ID | Requirement | Verified by |
|---|---|---|
| WALK-1 | A walk has at least 3 public stops, located at street or building precision, all within about 3 km. A private home is never a stop. | Generator tests |
| WALK-2 | Whether each stop still stands is checked through SerpApi Maps, and only checked stops are counted. | Eval D counts |
| WALK-3 | The assignment sheet prints cleanly and works offline. | A print-to-PDF snapshot |

## 3. Non-functional requirements
| ID | Requirement | Verified by |
|---|---|---|
| NFR-SEC-1 | No secret appears in the repo, in logs, or in recorded sessions. A secret scanner runs in CI, and the Entire checkpoints are scanned before the repo goes public. | CI, plus a scan report |
| NFR-SEC-2 | API input validation, a simple rate limit, and a dependency audit. | Tests, plus an audit report |
| NFR-PRIV-1 | No accounts, no tracking analytics and no session replay. The only thing stored on the device is the lights preference. | Code review, plus the e2e network log |
| NFR-REL-1 | The ingest and the investigation both survive a killed worker (kill tests 1 and 2). | Screenshots, plus counters |
| NFR-PERF-1 | Core Web Vitals are "good" on a mid-range phone profile. Initial JS stays under 200 KB gzipped, with the map loaded lazily. | Lighthouse, plus a bundle report |
| NFR-A11Y-1 | WCAG 2.2 AA: reading-text contrast of at least 4.5:1 in both modes, a visible blue-pencil focus style, full keyboard use, reduced motion respected, semantic headings. | axe, a contrast script, plus a keyboard e2e test |
| NFR-REPRO-1 | Every number shown anywhere comes from a script. `make numbers` regenerates the numbers sheet, with the command behind each number. | The numbers sheet diffs clean |
| NFR-COST-1 | Only free tiers and existing credits are used. Every run logs its cost. SerpApi use stays within budget. | Cost logs |
| NFR-OBS-1 | Both Sentry projects receive events, and releases are tagged with the git SHA. | The Sentry API |
| NFR-TEST-1 | Unit tests (lexicon, crop URLs, quote verifier, geocoder, schemas), integration tests (Temporal test environment), contract tests (API) and e2e tests (Playwright) all run from `make test`. | CI |
| NFR-LIC-1 | AmericanStories (CC-BY-4.0), GeoNames (CC-BY), the LoC scans, the OpenStreetMap and OpenFreeMap attribution, the font licences and the React Bits licence are all credited on the method page and in the README. | Review |

## 4. Constraints
- **Machine:** Apple M4 with 10 cores, 24 GB of RAM, and about 35 GB of free disk (measured Oct 29). No Docker.
- **Installed tools:** `uv`, Node and `pnpm`, the Temporal CLI with its dev server, Ollama (with `gemma4:26b-a4b-it-qat` and smaller Gemma 4 variants already pulled), `gh` and `entire`. Nothing is installed globally; project dependencies go through `uv` and `pnpm`.
- **Keys:** `.env` holds them; check them by shape only. The names are listed in `BRIEF.md`; the Ultramarine key is `PAPERINSTRUMENTS_API_KEY`. `GEMINI_API_KEY`, `ELEVENLABS_API_KEY` and `TABPFN_TOKEN` are present but unused.
- **Atlas:** the existing cluster. Its tier and storage limit are recorded in Phase 1.

## 5. Data requirements
- **Schemas:** `ARCHITECTURE.md` section 4. Pydantic is the source; Atlas validators are generated from it.
- **Stable IDs:**
  - A report is `r_` plus its primary article ID.
  - A case is `c_` plus its report ID.
  - A place is its GeoNames ID.
- **Every derived record** carries the versions that made it (lexicon, prompt, model or adapter, code SHA).
- **Dates** are ISO 8601. `month_day` is `MM-DD`, used by "Printed on this night".
- **Text:** the OCR text is stored as printed and is never corrected in place. A cleaned transcription, if one is shown, is stored separately and labelled.

## 6. API contract (read-only)
| Method and path | Returns |
|---|---|
| `GET /api/health` | `{ok, atlas, version}` |
| `GET /api/places?q=&state=` | Matching towns: `{place_id, name, state, report_count, years}` |
| `GET /api/towns/{place_id}` | The drawer: the place, its count line, and its reports `{id, date, paper, label, outcome, precision, location}` |
| `GET /api/reports/{id}` | The full case page payload: the report, plus its case if one exists |
| `GET /api/search?q=&state=&decade=&page=` | Text-search hits with a snippet, and the misread spellings each hit matched, e.g. `{scanned: "appariiion", term: "apparition"}` |
| `GET /api/near?lat=&lon=&km=` | Reports near a rounded point. The coordinates are never logged. |
| `GET /api/reports/{id}/similar?k=` | Vector-search neighbours |
| `GET /api/tonight?md=MM-DD` | Reports printed on that month and day |
| `GET /api/stats/reel` | Per-year and per-state series |
| `GET /api/walks/{place_id}` | A walk (P2 only) |

Errors take the form `{"error": {"code", "message"}}`. The core path is mirrored as static JSON (`ARCHITECTURE.md` section 3.6), so the site works while the API sleeps.

## 7. Evaluation specifications
Results are saved as JSON plus a chart under `eval/results/`, and each is produced by one command.

### 7.1 Evals A to D
- **A, the archive read:**
  - pages and articles read, and candidates per year
  - reports per million articles, by year and by state
  - the term mix and an OCR-quality distribution
  - prefilter recall: a random-sample upper bound (rule of three when no misses are found) and the misses found in the near-miss pool, with the lexicon changes they caused
- **B, the reader:**
  - kind accuracy and macro-F1, and report precision, recall and F1
  - field match rates, and the share of quotes verified
  - the hallucinated-quote rate
  - cost per 10,000 articles and latency
  - bootstrap 95% intervals throughout
  - the headline is the accuracy gap and the cost per 10,000 articles
- **C, the investigations:** case files written, named deaths found, cases explained or exposed, then-and-now differences, the claim-verification rate and dropped claims, and Gemma against Ultramarine on the same cases (claims, verification rate, cost, latency).
- **D, the app:** Lighthouse on mobile, axe, contrast, e2e on phone and desktop in both modes, and the walks counts if walks are built.

### 7.2 Reader ablations
| ID | What changes | Why it matters |
|---|---|---|
| B1 | Base 4B, tuned 4B, teacher | The headline comparison |
| B2 | Training set size (a learning curve of at least 3 points) | Whether more teacher labels would help |
| B3 | LoRA rank and learning rate (a small grid, within credits) | Picks the trained model |
| B4 | Output format: fields with quotes against kind only | The cost of grounding |
| B5 | Quote verifier on and off, plus a threshold sweep | Precision of the fields shown |
| B6 | Triage on and off | Reports lost against cost saved |
| B7 | Slices by OCR quality | Robustness to rough scans |
| B8 | Slices by decade | Language drift from 1774 to 1963 |
| B9 | Base 4B zero-shot against few-shot | Makes the baseline fair |
| B10 | Reprint leakage removed, or not | Proves the scores aren't inflated |

Model selection uses a dev split. The gold set is used only for these final runs.

### 7.3 Edge-case suite
Each slice uses at least 5 gold items where the archive has them:
- E1: sermons and hymns about the Holy Ghost
- E2: idioms ("ghost of a chance", "gave up the ghost", "not the ghost of a")
- E3: ghost stories as fiction, serials and Christmas stories
- E4: theatre and illusion adverts (Pepper's ghost), patent medicine and real estate
- E5: spiritualist séances and rappings (`POLICY.md` decides their kind)
- E6: hoax exposures and pranksters caught
- E7: humour and joke columns
- E8: phantom ships, trains and lights
- E9: one story reprinted under different datelines
- E10: badly garbled OCR
- E11: segmentation errors, where several items are merged into one article
- E12: non-English text
- E13: "Ghost" as a surname or a place name
- E14: political figures of speech ("the ghost of the tariff")

## 8. Traceability
| Requirements | Phase | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Environment, CI, skeleton | 1 | `eval/results/phase1_env.json`, CI run, skeleton screenshot |
| ING-*, eval A | 2A | `eval/results/archive_read.json`, kill test 1, crop check |
| GEO-*, DB-1 to DB-3 | 2B | `make db-init`, storage report, parser tests |
| RDR-*, eval B | 2C | `eval/results/reader_*.json`, `eval/MODEL_CARD.md` |
| DB-4 to DB-6, INV-2 | 2D | `make db-verify`, `eval/results/clustering.json`, harvest manifests |
| INV-*, eval C | 3A | Case files, kill test 2, Sentry traces |
| API-* | 3B | Contract tests, `eval/results/api_latency.json` |
| WEB-*, NFR-A11Y, NFR-PERF | 4 | e2e, axe, Lighthouse, screenshots |
| NFR-*, the numbers sheet, launch | 5 | `make numbers`, README, scan report, the post draft |

1	# Build plan
2	
3	How the build runs: five phases, each split into milestones, each milestone with a persona, deliverables and an exit gate. An engineering manager (EM) session writes the prompt for each milestone, a build session carries it out, and the EM checks the result before the next milestone starts.
4	
5	## 1. How each milestone runs
6	1. **The EM sends the milestone prompt:** its scope, its deliverables, and the gate it must pass.
7	2. **The build session works on a branch** named `phase-<n>-<slug>`.
8	   - Small commits, pushed to the private repo, with a pull request into `main`.
9	   - It ends with a STATUS block in `RESUME.md`.
10	   - Its final message starts with one line: `<milestone>: GATE PASSED` or `<milestone>: BLOCKED — <reason>`.
11	3. **The EM reviews:**
12	   - reads the diff, and re-runs the gate commands
13	   - spot-checks outputs against their sources, using a random sample
14	   - checks the non-negotiables: no secrets, no invented numbers, verified quotes, respect for the dead
15	   - checks that CI is green
16	4. **Pass:** the EM merges the pull request and sends the next prompt. **Fail:** the EM sends a numbered fix list, and the gate runs again.
17	5. **Owner gates** always stop and ask first: making the repo public, deploying, DNS, posting anywhere, and spending money.
18	
19	## 2. Phases and how they map to `BRIEF.md`
20	| Phase | Persona | `BRIEF.md` step | Milestones |
21	|---|---|---|---|
22	| 1 Scaffolding and environment | Systems architect, DevOps | Step 1, the setup part | 1 |
23	| 2 Database, schemas and data models | Data engineer, data architect, ML specialist | Step 1 (archive read), Step 2, Step 3 | 2A archive read and EDA; 2B schemas and data layer; 2C reader; 2D load, cluster and harvest |
24	| 3 Backend and APIs | Software engineer, ML specialist | Step 4, plus the API part of Step 5 | 3A investigator; 3B API and static export |
25	| 4 Frontend and integration | UI and UX specialist, software engineer, product manager | Step 5 | 4A brand and design system; 4B pages and integration; 4C deploy (owner's yes); 4D walks (owner's call) |
26	| 5 Polish and QA | QA engineer, DevOps, product manager | Step 6 | 5A QA and hardening; 5B launch assets and the post |
27	
28	## 3. Phase 1: scaffolding and environment
29	**Persona:** systems architect and DevOps engineer.
30	
31	**Deliverables**
32	- The planning docs and repo config committed.
33	- The repo layout from `ARCHITECTURE.md` section 5, the `uv` project, and the `pnpm` web shell.
34	- A Makefile. Targets that belong to later phases exist as stubs that say which phase builds them.
35	- `config.py`, plus `make keys`: a shape check for every key and one cheap authenticated call per service, printing only the name, OK, FAIL or EMPTY, and a reason.
36	- The Temporal dev server (`make temporal`, persisting under `data/temporal/`), a worker, and a smoke workflow with a heartbeat and a retry policy (`make smoke`).
37	- Environment facts, written by a script to `eval/results/phase1_env.json`:
38	  - Tinker: credits, the base models available for LoRA training and sampling, and whether trained weights can be downloaded
39	  - Atlas: tier, version, storage limit and storage used, and whether Atlas Search and Vector Search indexes can be created (create one of each on a scratch collection, then drop it)
40	  - Sentry: one test event sent, then read back through the API
41	  - SerpApi: searches left, read from the account endpoint
42	  - Ultramarine: one minimal call, with the model ID and the cost or usage it reports
43	  - Ollama: tokens per second for `gemma4:26b-a4b-it-qat`
44	  - the machine: cores, RAM and free disk
45	  - for `faro_1850`: download speed, plus parse speed in pages and articles per second on one core
46	- A walking skeleton: one real 1850 article (the Stratford, Conn. "knockings" report from the first probe) goes into a scratch Atlas collection, out through an API endpoint, and onto a web page that shows the IIIF crop next to the text.
47	- CI on GitHub Actions: `ruff`, offline `pytest`, a web typecheck and build, and a secret scan.
48	- Sentry init helpers for the API and the pipeline. They do nothing when no DSN is set, and they send no PII.
49	- A README skeleton, numbered entries in `DECISIONS.md`, and a STATUS block in `RESUME.md`.
50	
51	**Exit gate**
52	- `make setup`, `make keys`, `make smoke` and `make test` pass. The output of `make keys` contains no secret values.
53	- CI is green on the pull request.
54	- `git ls-files` shows no `.env` and no `Docs/IDEAS.md`, and the secret scan is clean.
55	- The skeleton page shows the real crop, and the crop matches its text.
56	- `phase1_env.json` was produced by a script, and the numbers in `RESUME.md` match it.
57	- `entire status` shows Entire enabled.
58	
59	## 4. Phase 2: database, schemas and data models
60	
61	### 2A: archive read and EDA
62	**Persona:** data engineer, with a systems specialist for throughput.
63	- Lexicon v1, with OCR variants and unit tests, plus a near-miss lexicon.
64	- `IngestArchiveWorkflow` over all 180 files: candidates, counts, samples and manifests, with concurrency set from Phase 1's measurements.
65	- Kill test 1, with Temporal UI screenshots from before and after.
66	- The crop check on 50 random candidates spread across batches.
67	- Eval A, with charts:
68	  - per year: pages, articles and candidates, and candidates per million articles
69	  - by state, the term mix and the OCR-quality distribution
70	  - the reprint signal, and candidate lengths
71	- Prefilter recall: the random-sample bound and the near-miss pool. If misses are found, lexicon v2 and a re-run.
72	
73	**Gate**
74	- All 180 years are done, or each failure is listed with its reason.
75	- Disk use is reported.
76	- `make ingest YEARS=1850` reproduces the 1850 counts exactly.
77	- Kill-test evidence exists, and every crop-check failure is explained.
78	- The EM spot-checks 20 random candidates and 10 random non-candidates against their sources.
79	
80	### 2B: schemas and data layer
81	**Persona:** data architect.
82	- Pydantic models, with Atlas validators generated from them.
83	- `make db-init` creates every collection and index, and can be re-run safely.
84	- A storage budget built from real document sizes, and a written decision on what goes into Atlas.
85	- The GeoNames geocoder and its manifest. The LCCN title parser, tested on at least 200 distinct titles.
86	- The reprint-clustering design, and its evaluation set.
87	
88	**Gate**
89	- Schema tests pass, and `make db-init` can run twice.
90	- The budget is written down.
91	- Geocoder accuracy is measured on a sample.
92	
93	### 2C: the reader
94	**Persona:** ML specialist.
95	1. Write `POLICY.md`, build the gold set, freeze it and hash it.
96	2. Build the labelling page.
97	3. Label the gold set before seeing any model output.
98	4. Teacher labels for the training pool, with the leakage check passing.
99	5. Baselines: a keyword rule, and base 4B both zero-shot and few-shot.
100	6. LoRA training on Tinker, iterating on the dev split until improvements stop. Each iteration is recorded.
101	7. Eval B, ablations B1 to B10, and edge-case slices E1 to E14.
102	8. The failure log, and `eval/MODEL_CARD.md`.
103	9. The local export and the offline proof.
104	10. The full pass over all triaged candidates.
105	
106	**Gate**
107	- The gold hash hasn't changed since the freeze, and the leakage check passes.
108	- The eval JSON and charts include confidence intervals.
109	- At least one failure is written up with its fix.
110	- The offline proof passes, and the full-pass counts are recorded.
111	- The EM audits 30 random reader outputs against their clippings.
112	
113	### 2D: load, cluster and harvest
114	**Persona:** data engineer.
115	- Geocode, cluster, embed, and load Atlas.
116	- `make db-verify` runs geo, fuzzy and vector queries and checks their expected results and latencies.
117	- The top-case rule, and the follow-up harvest as a second Temporal pass.
118	
119	**Gate**
120	- Atlas counts match the local counts, and storage is within the limit.
121	- `db-verify` passes.
122	- The harvest has written output for every case.
123	
124	## 5. Phase 3: backend and APIs
125	
126	### 3A: the investigator
127	**Persona:** software engineer and ML specialist.
128	- `InvestigateCaseWorkflow`, with Gemma 4 26B-A4B running locally as the default model and Ultramarine as the comparison run.
129	- Tools: archive search, death notices, SerpApi, and Wikipedia as the fallback.
130	- The guardrails, Sentry agent traces, and budget caps.
131	- Kill test 2, then 30–60 case files and eval C.
132	
133	**Gate**
134	- Kill test 2, by the counters: no completed paid call is repeated, and any call that was in flight at the kill is counted and reported.
135	- 100% of the claims kept are verified, and dropped claims are logged.
136	- Sentry traces carry tokens and cost.
137	- The Ultramarine comparison records the actual cost.
138	- The EM audits 5 case files end to end against their clippings.

# Build plan

How the build runs: five phases, each split into milestones, each milestone with a persona, deliverables and an exit gate. An engineering manager (EM) session writes the prompt for each milestone, a build session carries it out, and the EM checks the result before the next milestone starts.

## 1. How each milestone runs
1. **The EM sends the milestone prompt:** its scope, its deliverables, and the gate it must pass.
2. **The build session works on a branch** named `phase-<n>-<slug>`.
   - Small commits, pushed to the private repo, with a pull request into `main`.
   - It ends with a STATUS block in `RESUME.md`.
   - Its final message starts with one line: `<milestone>: GATE PASSED` or `<milestone>: BLOCKED — <reason>`.
3. **The EM reviews:**
   - reads the diff, and re-runs the gate commands
   - spot-checks outputs against their sources, using a random sample
   - checks the non-negotiables: no secrets, no invented numbers, verified quotes, respect for the dead
   - checks that CI is green
4. **Pass:** the EM merges the pull request and sends the next prompt. **Fail:** the EM sends a numbered fix list, and the gate runs again.
5. **Owner gates** always stop and ask first: making the repo public, deploying, DNS, posting anywhere, and spending money.

## 2. Phases and how they map to `BRIEF.md`
| Phase | Persona | `BRIEF.md` step | Milestones |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 Scaffolding and environment | Systems architect, DevOps | Step 1, the setup part | 1 |
| 2 Database, schemas and data models | Data engineer, data architect, ML specialist | Step 1 (archive read), Step 2, Step 3 | 2A archive read and EDA; 2B schemas and data layer; 2C reader; 2D load, cluster and harvest |
| 3 Backend and APIs | Software engineer, ML specialist | Step 4, plus the API part of Step 5 | 3A investigator; 3B API and static export |
| 4 Frontend and integration | UI and UX specialist, software engineer, product manager | Step 5 | 4A brand and design system; 4B pages and integration; 4C deploy (owner's yes); 4D walks (owner's call) |
| 5 Polish and QA | QA engineer, DevOps, product manager | Step 6 | 5A QA and hardening; 5B launch assets and the post |

## 3. Phase 1: scaffolding and environment
**Persona:** systems architect and DevOps engineer.

**Deliverables**
- The planning docs and repo config committed.
- The repo layout from `ARCHITECTURE.md` section 5, the `uv` project, and the `pnpm` web shell.
- A Makefile. Targets that belong to later phases exist as stubs that say which phase builds them.
- `config.py`, plus `make keys`: a shape check for every key and one cheap authenticated call per service, printing only the name, OK, FAIL or EMPTY, and a reason.
- The Temporal dev server (`make temporal`, persisting under `data/temporal/`), a worker, and a smoke workflow with a heartbeat and a retry policy (`make smoke`).
- Environment facts, written by a script to `eval/results/phase1_env.json`:
  - Tinker: credits, the base models available for LoRA training and sampling, and whether trained weights can be downloaded
  - Atlas: tier, version, storage limit and storage used, and whether Atlas Search and Vector Search indexes can be created (create one of each on a scratch collection, then drop it)
  - Sentry: one test event sent, then read back through the API
  - SerpApi: searches left, read from the account endpoint
  - Ultramarine: one minimal call, with the model ID and the cost or usage it reports
  - Ollama: tokens per second for `gemma4:26b-a4b-it-qat`
  - the machine: cores, RAM and free disk
  - for `faro_1850`: download speed, plus parse speed in pages and articles per second on one core
- A walking skeleton: one real 1850 article (the Stratford, Conn. "knockings" report from the first probe) goes into a scratch Atlas collection, out through an API endpoint, and onto a web page that shows the IIIF crop next to the text.
- CI on GitHub Actions: `ruff`, offline `pytest`, a web typecheck and build, and a secret scan.
- Sentry init helpers for the API and the pipeline. They do nothing when no DSN is set, and they send no PII.
- A README skeleton, numbered entries in `DECISIONS.md`, and a STATUS block in `RESUME.md`.

**Exit gate**
- `make setup`, `make keys`, `make smoke` and `make test` pass. The output of `make keys` contains no secret values.
- CI is green on the pull request.
- `git ls-files` shows no `.env` and no `Docs/IDEAS.md`, and the secret scan is clean.
- The skeleton page shows the real crop, and the crop matches its text.
- `phase1_env.json` was produced by a script, and the numbers in `RESUME.md` match it.
- `entire status` shows Entire enabled.

## 4. Phase 2: database, schemas and data models

### 2A: archive read and EDA
**Persona:** data engineer, with a systems specialist for throughput.
- Lexicon v1, with OCR variants and unit tests, plus a near-miss lexicon.
- `IngestArchiveWorkflow` over all 180 files: candidates, counts, samples and manifests, with concurrency set from Phase 1's measurements.
- Kill test 1, with Temporal UI screenshots from before and after.
- The crop check on 50 random candidates spread across batches.
- Eval A, with charts:
  - per year: pages, articles and candidates, and candidates per million articles
  - by state, the term mix and the OCR-quality distribution
  - the reprint signal, and candidate lengths
- Prefilter recall: the random-sample bound and the near-miss pool. If misses are found, lexicon v2 and a re-run.

**Gate**
- All 180 years are done, or each failure is listed with its reason.
- Disk use is reported.
- `make ingest YEARS=1850` reproduces the 1850 counts exactly.
- Kill-test evidence exists, and every crop-check failure is explained.
- The EM spot-checks 20 random candidates and 10 random non-candidates against their sources.

### 2B: schemas and data layer
**Persona:** data architect.
- Pydantic models, with Atlas validators generated from them.
- `make db-init` creates every collection and index, and can be re-run safely.
- A storage budget built from real document sizes, and a written decision on what goes into Atlas.
- The GeoNames geocoder and its manifest. The LCCN title parser, tested on at least 200 distinct titles.
- The reprint-clustering design, and its evaluation set.

**Gate**
- Schema tests pass, and `make db-init` can run twice.
- The budget is written down.
- Geocoder accuracy is measured on a sample.

### 2C: the reader
**Persona:** ML specialist.
1. Write `POLICY.md`, build the gold set, freeze it and hash it.
2. Build the labelling page.
3. Label the gold set before seeing any model output.
4. Teacher labels for the training pool, with the leakage check passing.
5. Baselines: a keyword rule, and base 4B both zero-shot and few-shot.
6. LoRA training on Tinker, iterating on the dev split until improvements stop. Each iteration is recorded.
7. Eval B, ablations B1 to B10, and edge-case slices E1 to E14.
8. The failure log, and `eval/MODEL_CARD.md`.
9. The local export and the offline proof.
10. The full pass over all triaged candidates.

**Gate**
- The gold hash hasn't changed since the freeze, and the leakage check passes.
- The eval JSON and charts include confidence intervals.
- At least one failure is written up with its fix.
- The offline proof passes, and the full-pass counts are recorded.
- The EM audits 30 random reader outputs against their clippings.

### 2D: load, cluster and harvest
**Persona:** data engineer.
- Geocode, cluster, embed, and load Atlas.
- `make db-verify` runs geo, fuzzy and vector queries and checks their expected results and latencies.
- The top-case rule, and the follow-up harvest as a second Temporal pass.

**Gate**
- Atlas counts match the local counts, and storage is within the limit.
- `db-verify` passes.
- The harvest has written output for every case.

## 5. Phase 3: backend and APIs

### 3A: the investigator
**Persona:** software engineer and ML specialist.
- `InvestigateCaseWorkflow`, with Gemma 4 26B-A4B running locally as the default model and Ultramarine as the comparison run.
- Tools: archive search, death notices, SerpApi, and Wikipedia as the fallback.
- The guardrails, Sentry agent traces, and budget caps.
- Kill test 2, then 30–60 case files and eval C.

**Gate**
- Kill test 2, by the counters: no completed paid call is repeated, and any call that was in flight at the kill is counted and reported.
- 100% of the claims kept are verified, and dropped claims are logged.
- Sentry traces carry tokens and cost.
- The Ultramarine comparison records the actual cost.
- The EM audits 5 case files end to end against their clippings.

### 3B: API and static export
**Persona:** software engineer.
- FastAPI endpoints from `SRS.md` section 6, with contract tests, Sentry, the privacy tests and latency measurements.
- `export_static`, plus the cached crops for the front page and the top cases.

**Gate**
- Tests are green, and the OpenAPI document is generated.
- Latency numbers are recorded.
- The export can be reproduced.

## 6. Phase 4: frontend and integration

### 4A: brand and design system
**Persona:** UI and UX specialist.
- **`Docs/BRAND.md`:** the name, voice, nameplate, mark, colours (a table of contrast-checked pairs), type, motion, materials, and do and don't.
- **Logo set:**
  - the nameplate in UnifrakturMaguntia, as SVG outlines
  - a rubber-stamp mark for small sizes
  - the favicon set
  - a social-card template built on a real clipping
- **Category assets (SVG):**
  - outcome stamps for unexplained, explained, hoax and unknown, with an ink filter
  - eight place-type glyphs in a 19th-century atlas engraving style
  - three precision pins
  - kind tags and decade frame markers
  - the envelope, the index card, the request slip, the scissor-edge mask, and **-30-**
- **Tokens:** CSS variables for both modes, the type scale, spacing, paper shadows and motion (heavy damping, no bounce).
- **The component library,** and a style-guide route that shows every component with real archive data.
- **The Halloween look** comes from the reading room after dark, as `UI-IDEAS.md` describes, and never from costume-shop iconography.

**Gate**
- The contrast script passes.
- The EM reviews style-guide screenshots in both modes and at phone width.
- The owner is shown the brand set before the page work begins.

### 4B: pages and integration
**Persona:** UI and UX specialist, software engineer, and product manager for the feature review.
- The front page, town drawer, case page, the reel, the method page and the 404, wired to the static JSON and the live API.
- The seven signature moments with their reduced-motion fallbacks, and the map.

**Gate**
- Playwright e2e passes on phone and desktop, in both modes.
- axe and Lighthouse pass, no request goes to Google Fonts, and the copy lint passes.
- The EM walks through towns with one report, many reports and none.

### 4C: deploy (owner's yes)
- `render.yaml`, the Atlas network-access change, environment variables, Sentry releases, and a smoke test on the live URL.

### 4D: walks (owner's call)
- `SRS.md` WALK-1 to WALK-3.

## 7. Phase 5: polish and QA

### 5A: QA and hardening
**Persona:** QA engineer and DevOps engineer.
- A full test pass, a regression list and fixes.
- Performance work, and a security review (secrets, CORS, dependency audit).
- The Entire checkpoint secret scan.
- The README: reproduction steps, "What it can't do", and the failure log.
- The numbers sheet, from `make numbers`.

### 5B: launch
**Persona:** product manager.
- Screenshots, GIFs and the launch video, following `/Users/hotragn/Documents/Claude Code/tools/brag/skills/brag-slim/SKILL.md`.
- The DEV post draft, following the template:
  - every section, including The Spirit of It
  - My Agent Session, from Entire
  - the prize categories
- The EM reviews the draft against the judging rubric.

**Final gate: the judging checklist**

1	# Product brief: Paper Ghosts
2	
3	A newspaper's archive of old clippings is called its morgue. Paper Ghosts is a morgue for every ghost that America's newspapers reported between 1774 and 1963.
4	
5	## What it is
6	You type a town and get the real ghost reports printed in or about that town. They come straight from old newspapers, not from legends retold on the web. Each report shows:
7	- **the original clipping**, cropped from the Library of Congress page scan, next to its transcription
8	- the paper, date and place, plus who saw what and where
9	- **what happened next**: follow-up stories, the debunking, the arrest of the prankster, the family that moved out
10	- **the person behind the ghost**, when a name leads to a real death notice or inquest in the same papers
11	- **then and now**: what the 1890s paper said, next to what today's web and ghost tours say about the same place
12	
13	The site never writes a ghost story. Everything it shows was printed in a newspaper, and every claim links to the clipping it came from.
14	
15	**Walks: an optional layer, built only after the core works.** Search stays the front door. On top of it:
16	- **Near me:** a map of reports around you. Your location is rounded to about 1 km, used for that one query and never logged.
17	- **Self-guided walks:** offered only where a town has at least 3 precisely located stops that the public can see from a street, all within about 3 km.
18	  - Each stop shows its clipping, what happened next, and what stands there now.
19	  - A walk can be saved as a printable page, so it works offline.
20	- **Road trips** across several towns: a stretch goal, and the first thing to cut.
21	
22	## Who it's for
23	Anyone curious about their own town on Halloween, plus local historians, genealogists and ghost-tour guides who want the original source rather than the retelling.
24	
25	## Non-negotiables
26	1. **Secrets:**
27	   - Keys live in `.env`. Never print, log, echo or commit them; read them through the environment only.
28	   - `.env` is already at the repo root, and `.gitignore` covers it. It holds `TINKER_API_KEY`, `MONGODB_URI` and `RENDER_API_KEY`, plus a few unused keys.
29	   - For Sentry it holds `SENTRY_DSN` (API project), `SENTRY_DSN_WEB` (web project), and `SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN` with `SENTRY_ORG` and `SENTRY_PROJECT`. The token can read events and traces, and write projects.
30	   - Optional keys the owner may fill in later: `SERPAPI_API_KEY`, `ULTRAMARINE_API_KEY` (with `ULTRAMARINE_BASE_URL` and `ULTRAMARINE_MODEL`), and `HF_TOKEN`. An empty value means the service isn't set up. Nothing in the build may wait on them.
31	   - Check every key by shape only (prefix, length, a test call), never by printing it.
32	2. **No fake anything:**
33	   - No invented results, users, quotes or numbers.
34	   - Every number in the README, results files or UI must come from a script in this repo and be reproducible with one command.
35	   - Approximations are labelled as approximations where they appear.
36	3. **Sources, not stories:**
37	   - The model only reads, classifies and quotes.
38	   - Every extracted field carries a verbatim quote from the article. Code checks the quote against the source text, with fuzzy matching for OCR noise.
39	   - A field without a verified quote shows as "not stated", never as a guess.
40	   - No generated fiction anywhere in the product.
41	4. **Respect the dead:**
42	   - These were real people. No mockery, and no guessing at causes of death beyond what the papers printed.
43	   - When the investigator links a ghost to a death, it shows both clippings and states how sure the link is.
44	   - Walks never send anyone onto private property. A private home is never a stop.
45	   - Every pin says how precise its location is: town, street or building.
46	5. **Quality bar:**
47	   - Premium and restrained, with real typography. The visual direction comes from the owner's `Docs/UI-IDEAS.md`, and the real scans are the only imagery.
48	   - No Halloween clip art, no emoji soup, no generic gradient "AI app" look, no filler copy.
49	   - Fast on a phone: lazy-load the clipping images.
50	6. **Honest limits are written down:** the README gets a "What it can't do" section, plus a log of failures found.
51	7. **Anything public waits for the owner's yes.** Stop and ask before any of these:
52	   - making the repo public
53	   - deploying under the owner's accounts
54	   - pointing the domain
55	   - posting anywhere or messaging anyone
56	   - spending money beyond free tiers and existing credits
57	8. **Start fresh.** Don't copy code from `week2/` or `week3/`. Reading them for patterns is fine.
58	
59	## Data (verified 2026-10-29)
60	**AmericanStories** (Hugging Face `dell-research-harvard/AmericanStories`, CC-BY-4.0, from Harvard's Dell Research): article-level text extracted from the Library of Congress's Chronicling America scans.
61	- **Files:** 180 per-year files, `faro_{year}.tar.gz`, 340 GB in total.
62	  - Download: `https://huggingface.co/datasets/dell-research-harvard/AmericanStories/resolve/main/faro_{year}.tar.gz`
63	  - Sizes: 1850 is 0.99 GB; 1897–1920 are 6–7.6 GB each.
64	- **Format:** each tar member is one page scan, as JSON:
65	  - `lccn`: `{title, state, lccn, …}`, where `title` includes the place of publication, e.g. "The New York herald. [volume] (New York [N.Y.]) 1840-1920"
66	  - `edition`: `{date}`
67	  - `scan`: `{width, height, raw_data_loc}`
68	  - `full articles`: a list of `{headline, article, byline, bbox, bbox_list, id, full_article_id}`
69	- **Machine limits:**
70	  - Download speed measured 66 MB/s, so a full pass is about 1.5 h of transfer.
71	  - Only **37 GB of disk is free**. Stream every file and never store the tarballs.
72	- **First probe (1850):** 733,880 articles, 1,018 mentioning ghosts and 33 strong reports, among them the Phelps family "knockings" in Stratford, Conn. The OCR is rough in places.
73	
74	**Page scans for the clippings** (public domain, Library of Congress IIIF image service):
75	- `raw_data_loc` looks like `https://chroniclingamerica.loc.gov/data/batches/{batch}/data/{lccn}/{reel}/{issue}/{seq}.jp2`.
76	- The crop is `https://tile.loc.gov/image-services/iiif/service:ndnp:{awardee}:batch_{batch}:data:{lccn}:{reel}:{issue}:{seq}/{x},{y},{w},{h}/pct:50/0/default.jpg`, where:
77	  - `awardee` is the first part of the batch name (`dlc_marcus_ver01` gives `dlc`)
78	  - `bbox` is `[x1, y1, x2, y2]` in scan pixels, so `w = x2-x1` and `h = y2-y1`
79	- This was verified on one 1850 New York Herald article, and the crop matched the text. Verify it across many batches before relying on it.
80	- Use `bbox_list` for articles that run across columns.
81	
82	**Gone:** the old Chronicling America JSON API returns 404, so the dataset above is the source.
83	
84	**Places:** take the publication place from the `lccn` title, plus places named in the article. Geocode offline with GeoNames (`cities1000`, CC-BY), recording the source and retrieval date in a manifest.
85	
86	## Stack (each tool has a real job, and each job needs proof: a screenshot, a number, or a failure it caught)
87	**Tinker is the main tool, and the depth goes there.** The others support it with one job each. The data layer is MongoDB Atlas (already set up), not Tiger Data. There is no .tech domain.
88	- **Temporal:** durable runs. The 340 GB ingest is one workflow, with one activity per year file, heartbeats and retries. Investigations are workflows too, with retries on flaky tool calls.
89	  - Run Temporal locally with the CLI dev server.
90	  - Prove it twice, and capture the Temporal UI timeline both times:
91	    - Kill the worker mid-ingest.
92	    - Kill it mid-investigation. The investigator agent must resume at the same step without repeating paid model calls it already made.
93	  - The investigation is the main Temporal story: an agent whose every model call and tool call is a retried, resumable step.
94	- **Tinker:** the reader, a small model trained for this task.
95	  - A large teacher (Qwen3.5-397B, or the best available) labels candidate articles.
96	  - A small student (Qwen3.5-4B, LoRA) learns from those labels.
97	  - Measure the base student, the tuned student and the teacher on a held-out gold set: accuracy, cost per 10,000 articles and latency.
98	  - The tuned student is the model that reads the whole archive, and it must also run locally offline.
99	  - Record at least one failure the eval exposed and what changed because of it. For example, sermons about the Holy Ghost might be read as sightings.
100	- **MongoDB Atlas:** the data layer.
101	  - Geo queries for "near this town" and "near me", and for building walks.
102	  - Atlas Search with fuzzy matching, because OCR turns "apparition" into "appariiion".
103	  - Atlas Vector Search for "ghosts like this one", with an open embedding model.
104	  - The investigators' case files.
105	  - Check the cluster's storage limit first, and keep the bulk candidate files local if it is small.
106	- **The investigator:** for each top case, it works through a pile of related old articles (follow-ups, death notices, inquests, debunkings) and writes a case file in which every claim cites a clipping.
107	  - By default it runs on an open-weight model (local Gemma 4 26B through Ollama, or the Tinker teacher), so nothing waits on a new account.
108	  - When an Ultramarine key exists (Paper Instruments' model, called through the OpenAI or Anthropic SDK), run the same cases on it, compare the case files, and record what each run actually cost.
109	- **SerpApi (when its key exists):** live web search for the investigator. Is the house still standing, and what do today's legend and ghost tours claim? This produces the then-and-now cards.
110	  - The free plan is 250 searches a month, so budget them.
111	  - Until the key exists, use Wikipedia's public API for the "now" side, and say so on the card.
112	  - For walk stops, use its Google Maps results to check whether the place still stands, and to get its coordinates and opening hours.
113	- **Sentry:** traces of investigator and reader runs, covering latency, tokens and cost per case.
114	  - Two projects already exist in org `hotragn`: `paperghosts-api` (Python, FastAPI) and `paperghosts-web` (React).
115	  - Sentry is linked to the GitHub repo `Hotragn/Paperghosts`, so releases and suspect commits can work.
116	  - Use `SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN` to pull real trace numbers for the write-up. Keep only the traces that explain a real bug or bottleneck, and write up that story in `DECISIONS.md`.
117	- **Render:** hosts the site and the API. The owner approves the deploy.
118	- **Optional, only if time allows and it does real work:**
119	  - Entire, to capture the agent sessions behind the build. It's already enabled in this repo, so every build session is recorded. Before the repo goes public, scan the recorded sessions for secrets.
120	  - Gemma, to re-read the scan image when the OCR is unreadable.
121	  - Backboard, to compare open models through one key before training.
122	
123	## Depth requirements (each has an eval or test, saved under `eval/results/` as JSON plus a chart)
